# SOP-P3-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, MM-P3-L4-RR01

Purpose
1. To define the standardized shift handover process for the Heat Treat line (P3-L4), ensuring continuity of operations, safe condition of equipment, and accurate transfer of process and maintenance information between operators.

Background and rationale
2. The Heat Treat line includes the re-rolling coil unit EQ-P3-L4-RR01, the heat treat furnace EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and the shot blast cabinet EQ-P3-L4-SB03. Operational continuity is essential to avoid scrapped parts, quality deviations, and unsafe conditions. Handover must communicate process state, pending actions, issues, and recent maintenance per ECN-2026-001 and machine maintenance procedures MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01. Documented handovers reduce miscommunication and support traceability for audits and root cause analysis.

Preconditions (required before handover)
3. The outgoing operator shall complete: verification of process parameters per MM-P3-L4-HT02, completion of any lockout/tagout per ECN-2026-001 if maintenance occurred, and confirmation that all critical tools and spares are in the designated locations. Any active maintenance tags must reference MM-P3-L4-RR01 or MM-P3-L4-HT02 as applicable.

PPE (minimum for handover walkdown)
4. Outgoing and incoming personnel must wear required PPE for line access and walkdown: ear protection, eye protection, protective footwear, and heat-resistant gloves when opening furnace guards. If entering confined or hot zones, follow PPE per MM-P3-L4-HT02.

Handover steps (numbered sequence)
5. Outgoing operator prepares handover notes
   5.1. Record the current job/lot identifier and part code as per the production board.  
   5.2. Note any deviations, rejects, or process parameter excursions and reference the corrective action or temporary workaround. Cite any engineering change requests to ECN-2026-001 if applicable.  
   5.3. List active maintenance work orders or outstanding issues that require follow-up and reference MM-P3-L4-HT02 or MM-P3-L4-RR01.

6. Line status walkdown with incoming operator
   6.1. Conduct a physical walkdown of EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 together. Show current mode (running, standby, or locked out) and location of the last processed piece.  
   6.2. Point out any abnormal sounds, leaks, or visible wear. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03, show the blast wheel and liner access panels and the condition of the blast media. Ensure the incoming operator understands the location of spares and the lubricant spares box.

7. Critical maintenance and lubrication information
   7.1. Confirm next planned maintenance and any deferred items against MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01 records.  
   7.2. For EQ-P3-L4-SB03: confirm lubricant part and fastener information. The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is 90 N·m. Record when these were last checked and whether any fasteners were loosened during the shift.

8. Safety-critical items and alarms
   8.1. Demonstrate recent alarm history on EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and EQ-P3-L4-RR01. Explain root-cause status for any recurring alarms and the mitigation in place. Reference troubleshooting steps in MM-P3-L4-HT02.  
   8.2. Confirm emergency stop circuits and access to local isolators. If any isolator is tagged out, ensure the tag references ECN-2026-001 and the associated work order.

9. Material and quality transfer
   9.1. Show incoming operator the inventory of in-process material, quarantined parts, and any parts under inspection. Note any quality hold and the reason.  
   9.2. Transfer any sample pieces for incoming operator inspection and note where process data and logs are stored.

10. Examples and typical notes to include
   10.1. Example entry: "Lot XYZ in EQ-P3-L4-HT02 paused at chamber 2; furnace ramp complete; awaiting QA sign-off."  
   10.2. Example entry: "EQ-P3-L4-SB03 blast media judgement: requires top-up; liner bolts checked—no movement; lubricant on hand: CFW-LUB-526."  
   10.3. Use concise, factual entries; avoid subjective language.

11. Records to keep
   11.1. Outgoing operator shall upload the signed handover log to the line control folder and retain a paper copy in the shift binder.  
   11.2. Record references to ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, and MM-P3-L4-RR01 where relevant. Include timestamps and operator signatures.

12. Sign-off and acceptance
   12.1. Incoming operator shall read the handover notes, complete a walkdown with the outgoing operator, and confirm acceptance by signing the handover log.  
   12.2. If the incoming operator cannot accept the line due to unresolved safety or quality issues, escalate to the shift lead and annotate the reason in the log. Reference MM-P3-L4-HT02 or MM-P3-L4-RR01 for escalation steps.

Roles and responsibilities
13. Outgoing operator: prepare accurate notes, perform complete walkdown, verify maintenance tags and PPE compliance.  
14. Incoming operator: review notes, perform independent verification, accept or escalate.  
15. Shift lead: adjudicate disputes, approve transfer of responsibility, ensure records are filed.

Change control and references
16. Any procedural changes that affect handover content or responsibilities must be proposed through ECN-2026-001. Maintenance requirements are governed by MM-P3-L4-HT02 and MM-P3-L4-RR01.

Appendix: audit and verification guidance
17. Auditors should verify that handover logs contain: job/lot identifier, any active maintenance references, lubricant confirmation for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 as CFW-LUB-526, and that the blast wheel liner bolt torque for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is recorded as 90 N·m when applicable. Ensure handover logs cite ECN-2026-001, MM-P3-L4-HT02, and MM-P3-L4-RR01 where maintenance or engineering changes are involved.

Sign-off
18. Handover complete when both operators sign the handover log and the incoming operator assumes control of P3-L4 line operations.
